claim: Let R and W_int be the explicit 4x5 matrices below. R and its Bob partial transpose are PSD, and Tr(W_int R)=-18. W_int has integer entries and, for every 4x5 coefficient matrix X of rank at most two, <X|W_int|X> >= (6/11)||X||_F^2. Consequently W_int is the Choi matrix of an explicit strictly 2-positive, indecomposable map M_4 -> M_5 that detects the explicit PPT state R/31 with expectation -18/31. The entire 2-block-positivity inequality is proved below; it is NOT inferred from numerical sampling or an SOS search. This does not itself construct a 4x4 PPT Schmidt-number-three state.
source_state: In C^4 tensor C^5 write [v]=|v><v| and set A=|00>+|11>+|22>, B=|01>+|12>, D=|10>-|21>, C=|02>+|34>, E=|20>+|33>, F=|23>, G=|30>, I=|32>, H=|04>. These nine vectors are pairwise orthogonal. Put R=[A]+[B]+[D]+3([C]+[E]+[F]+[G]+[I]+[H]). The exact Fraction/Schur checker records PSD ranks 9 and 10 for R and R^Gamma, and Tr R=31. This is the explicit 4x5 construction from Krebs-Gachechiladze arXiv:2509.07086v1, Theorem 5, with Bob second.
witness: Let P_R be the orthogonal projector onto span(A,B,D,C,E,F,G,I,H), let P_K=I_20-P_R, and let P_K0=P_R-[A]/3, the orthogonal projector onto span(B,D,C,E,F,G,I,H). Define the integer Hermitian matrix W_int=18*10^11*P_K + 18*P_K0 - 58*[A]. The projectors are completely explicit: P_R=[A]/3+([B]+[D]+[C]+[E])/2+[F]+[G]+[I]+[H]. Every entry of W_int is an integer. Its exact pairing with R is 18*28-58*9=-18, since Tr(P_K R)=0, Tr(P_K0 R)=28 and Tr([A]R)=9.
rank_identity: For a general vector Y in range(R), write its 4x5 coefficient matrix as Psi=[[a,b,c,0,h],[d,a,b,0,0],[e,-d,a,f,0],[g,0,i,e,c]]. Let M[r1r2r3|c1c2c3] be the corresponding 3x3 determinant in zero-based Alice and Bob indices. The exact identity, checked by expansion with integer/Fraction coefficients, is a^4=a*M[012|012]-a*M[013|123]-a*M[123|014]-(c/2)*M[013|013]-(e/2)*M[123|124]. It holds for complex variables as a polynomial identity.
determinant_perturbation: Take any rank<=2 matrix X with ||X||_F=1; set Y=P_R X and E_0=X-Y, with u=||E_0||_F. Every 3x3 minor of X vanishes. For each of the five minors in the identity, telescope det(Y)-det(X) one column at a time. Each of the three terms has one column from E_0 and two columns from X or Y, so by Hadamard its modulus is at most u, since ||X||_F=1 and ||Y||_F<=1. Therefore every cited minor of Y has modulus <=3u. Orthogonality of the source basis gives |a|,|c|,|e|<=1. Setting t=|a|, the identity and triangle inequality yield t^4 <= 3u(3|a|+|c|/2+|e|/2) <= 12u, hence t^8 <= 144u^2.
rank_two_margin_proof: Let s^2=||P_K0 X||_F^2 and alpha=1/10^11. Orthogonal decomposition gives 1=u^2+3t^2+s^2. Since <A,X>=3a, the normalized operator W_alpha=W_int/(18*10^11) satisfies <X|W_alpha|X>=u^2+alpha(s^2-29t^2). If s^2>=30t^2, then s^2-29t^2>=s^2/30 and 1<=u^2+(11/10)s^2; using alpha<=33 gives <X|W_alpha|X> >= (alpha/33)(u^2+(11/10)s^2) >= alpha/33. If s^2<30t^2 but u^2>=1/2, then the same expectation is at least 1/2-29alpha >= alpha/33. Finally, if s^2<30t^2 and u^2<1/2, the norm identity gives t^2>1/66, and the determinant bound gives u^2>1/(144*66^4); therefore the expectation exceeds 1/(144*66^4)-29alpha >= alpha/33. The last two scalar comparisons are exact rational assertions in the checker. Scaling by 18*10^11 gives the claimed 6/11 margin for every unit rank<=2 X, and homogeneity gives it for all such X.
map_convention: The Choi map is defined by Phi_W(|i><j|)=sum_(b,d=0)^4 (W_int)_(i,b;j,d)|b><d|. The standard Choi/block-positivity equivalence says W_int is 2-block positive iff Phi_W is 2-positive; indeed an arbitrary test vector for (id_2 tensor Phi_W)(|v><v|) yields the expectation of W_int on a vector of Schmidt rank at most two. The positive 6/11 margin also means Phi_W-(6/11)Tr(.)I_5 is 2-positive. A decomposable map's Choi witness cannot have negative expectation on a PPT state, so this explicit map is indecomposable.
